featured.title: Iran Crisis Keeps Strait of Hormuz at the Centre of Global Energy Markets
featured.content: Iran says the Strait of Hormuz will not reopen until conditions linked to its earlier diplomatic proposal are met. Meanwhile, Middle Eastern oil exports have recovered significantly, while the G7's emergency reserve release is adding supply to the market. The combination of recovering exports and continuing geopolitical and shipping risks is keeping crude prices close to $100 a barrel.

articles.title: Iran–US: Hormuz Remains a Major Flashpoint
articles.content: The diplomatic stalemate between Washington and Tehran continues, with Iran saying the Strait of Hormuz will not reopen until its conditions are met. The waterway remains strategically important for global energy and shipping. Reuters reports that Iranian officials have tied reopening the strait to conditions contained in an earlier interim agreement. The continuing uncertainty means any major disruption to shipping could quickly affect oil prices, freight costs and inflation.

articles.title: Oil Holds Near $100 as Supply Concerns Ease but Gulf Risks Remain
articles.content: Oil prices remain close to $100 a barrel. Brent was around $100.28 a barrel and US WTI around $89.33 in early Tuesday trading. Increased Middle Eastern exports and the G7's emergency stockpile plan have helped ease some supply concerns, but continuing attacks and uncertainty around Gulf shipping are limiting the decline. Reuters reports that Middle Eastern exports exceeded pre-war levels on several days during the final week of September.
articles.imageQuery: Brent crude oil barrels energy market

articles.title: France: Student Protests Enter a Tense Third Week
articles.content: High-school student protests in France continue over overcrowding, underfunding, deteriorating school conditions and pressure on students. Le Monde reports that 190 students have been injured since the protests began, while the Interior Ministry has reported about 650 injured police officers. Several investigations into alleged police violence are underway. The government is facing pressure to address both the underlying education concerns and violence surrounding some demonstrations.

articles.title: Nigeria: Military Aircraft Crash Kills 32
articles.content: A Nigerian military aircraft crashed in Ondo State on Monday while travelling from Benin City towards Lagos. Reuters reports that all 32 people aboard — 25 passengers and seven crew members — died. The wreckage was located near Igbokoda. President Bola Tinubu ordered an investigation into the cause of the crash. Authorities are expected to provide further details as the investigation continues.

articles.title: Nigeria: Security Forces Report Killing of Alleged ISWAP Commander
articles.content: Nigeria's State Security Service says a joint intelligence-led operation in Owo forest, Ondo State, killed Abdussamad Ohida, described by the agency as a senior ISWAP commander. Premium Times reports that the operation involved Nigerian security agencies and intelligence support from the United Kingdom. The allegations about Ohida's role in previous attacks are attributed to the SSS and remain part of the authorities' account of the operation.

articles.title: Nigeria: Voter Register Surpasses 103 Million Ahead of 2027 Elections
articles.content: Nigeria's Independent National Electoral Commission says the national register of voters has risen above 103 million following the completion of the three-phase Continuous Voter Registration exercise and biometric cleanup. INEC says nationwide collection of Permanent Voter Cards will begin on 9 October 2026. The commission has also acquired 57,000 new BVAS devices and says technological and logistical preparations are continuing ahead of the 2027 elections.

articles.title: Spain: Catalonia Flooding Leaves Deaths and Major Disruption
articles.content: Severe flooding caused by heavy rainfall in Catalonia has left at least two people dead and one person missing. Reuters reports that homes, roads and vehicles were affected and transport services were disrupted around Barcelona and other parts of the region. Authorities continue to monitor the situation and search for the missing person.

articles.title: G7 Emergency Oil Release Aims to Ease Global Fuel Pressure
articles.content: G7 countries have agreed to release up to 100 million barrels of diesel and crude from emergency reserves over four months, with the International Energy Agency coordinating the programme. The move comes as diesel shortages and disrupted energy logistics place pressure on transport and industry. The effect on consumer prices will depend on how quickly additional supplies reach markets.

articles.title: Nigeria: Dangote Refinery Remains Central to Fuel Security Debate
articles.content: Nigeria's Dangote Refinery remains a major part of the country's energy story as international oil prices and global supply disruptions continue to influence domestic fuel prices. The refinery's growing role in refined-product supply also gives Nigeria greater potential to participate in regional and international fuel markets. However, domestic pump prices remain exposed to international crude prices and wider logistics costs.

articles.title: Brazil: Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro Head to Presidential Runoff
articles.content: Brazil's presidential election is heading to a second round after Sunday's first-round vote failed to produce a candidate with more than 50% of valid votes. President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro will compete in the runoff. Reuters reports that Bolsonaro performed better than many pre-election expectations. The final outcome will be decided in the second round rather than by the first-round result.
articles.imageQuery: Brazil presidential election voting Lula Bolsonaro

articles.title: Japan: Tokyo Monitors Energy Markets
articles.content: Japan says it currently has no plans for another release of crude oil from its national reserves despite the coordinated G7 emergency-stockpile programme. Tokyo is continuing to monitor international energy markets as the Middle East crisis affects crude, refined products and shipping costs.

articles.title: Global Markets Watch Energy, Interest Rates and European Debt
articles.content: Global investors remain focused on energy prices, central-bank policy and geopolitical risks. European markets are also watching developments around France's public finances, while oil remains sensitive to both recovering Middle Eastern exports and the continuing security risks around Gulf infrastructure and shipping.

articles.title: Africa: Energy and Security Pressures Continue to Shape Economies
articles.content: African economies remain exposed to global energy prices, transport costs and security pressures. In Nigeria, higher fuel costs, the expansion of domestic refining and preparations for the 2027 elections are among the major issues attracting public attention. Across the continent, disruptions in international energy and food supply chains can quickly affect household costs and business activity.

morningSummary: The global agenda this Tuesday is dominated by the Iran–US conflict and its impact on energy markets. The Strait of Hormuz remains a major flashpoint, although Middle Eastern oil exports have recovered significantly and the G7 emergency reserve release is adding supplies to global markets. In Europe, France's student protests continue amid serious injuries and investigations. In Africa, Nigeria is dealing with the deaths of 32 people in a military aircraft crash, a reported counter-terrorism operation in Ondo State and preparations for the 2027 elections. Spain is also dealing with severe flooding in Catalonia, while Brazil is preparing for a presidential runoff.
